section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section reviews body image as a multifaceted construct and explores the relationship between interoception (internal bodily sensation processing) and body image. The text discusses multiple studies examining interoceptive sensitivity and awareness in relation to body dissatisfaction and positive body image across various populations including Norwegian high school students (N=82), Hungarian university students (N=70), British female university students (N=50), Austrian nonclinical participants (N=30 each for high and low cardiac perception groups), and Australian female university students (N=200). The section emphasizes that positive body image is distinct from the absence of negative body image and highlights the limited research on relationships between interoceptive processing and positive body image specifically.
